accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE Year 3 statutory wording (count up and down in tenths; tenths arise from dividing an object into 10 equal parts and dividing one-digit numbers by 10) and NCETM Year 3 ready-to-progress 3F-1. Every value is exact: 10/10 = 1, 3 ÷ 10 = 3/10, 12 tenths = 1 and 2/10, 23 tenths = 2 and 3/10, and the uneven bar's ten widths sum to exactly 1 so it is truly ten unequal parts. The 8-part bar is correctly called eighths.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented tenths errors from Ryan and Williams (2007) and the NCETM fractions guidance: adding denominators (4/10 + 1/10 = 5/20), counting 10 unequal parts as tenths, confusing a tenth with ten or a hundredth, writing 9/11 after 9/10, inverting a share as 10/3 or 1/3, and failing to regroup 15 tenths into 1 whole and 5 tenths.

lab_distinct.evidence: Five different mechanics: tap-to-shade a ten-part bar up to 10/10, a fair-or-not judgement on equal, unequal and eight-part bars, dragging a frog along a 0-1 tenths line to targets, sharing 1, 3 and 7 bars among 10 coloured children, and a wholes-and-tenths builder that auto-swaps 10 tenths for a whole. It is not the generic fracbar of lessons 09 and 11, and the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each task ends on the rule it showed: 'Ten tenths make 1 whole: 10/10 = 1', 'Tenths are 10 equal parts', 'Count on in tenths: 9/10, then 10/10 = 1', 'Share 7 bars between 10: 7/10 each' and '10 tenths swap for 1 whole'. The share step colours child 1's tenth in every bar, so 3/10 is seen as one tenth from each of 3 bars.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: what one of 10 equal parts is called ('One ten'), whether 10 unequal parts are tenths ('Yes, there are 10 parts'), where 9/10 plus a hop lands ('9/11' and '10/100'), and what each of 10 children gets from 3 bars ('1/3 of a bar'). The reveal line quotes the learner's guess against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions with fourteen tagged slips (ten, hund, one, hund2, addbot, bot1, unit, flip, uneven, eight, wholes, noswap, den, den2). Each names the error in the question's own numbers, for example 'Do not add the bottoms. They stay tenths: 4 tenths and 1 tenth is 5 tenths, 5/10.' and 'After 10 tenths make 1 whole, only 5 tenths are left'.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses a chocolate bar, short sentences and introduces 'top number' and 'bottom number' before any symbol; adult text names numerator and denominator and quotes the curriculum. Both are within the validator's FK limits. Canvas prompts split onto two lines on a 360 px phone instead of shrinking.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler-phrase scan and the 12% explanation-overlap gate against 09 Fraction Notation, 11 Understanding Fractions, 12 Fractions on a Number Line and 65 Fractions as Division. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (a tenth, top and bottom numbers, equal parts, counting to 10/10) with no restated summary.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on Android 360 px in dark and light and iPhone 13 light, before and after Show me on every step. The number line labels only even tenths plus the target on narrow screens so labels never collide, answer cards are about 100 x 70 px, and the wholes and tenths bars are 30 px tall with full-width button twins below.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA on desktop and iPhone 13 in light and dark with no violations and no console errors. Every canvas action has a button twin (Shade 1 more tenth, Tenths / Not tenths, Hop back and Hop on 1/10, Each child gets 3/10, +1 whole, +1 tenth, −1 tenth) and the canvas aria-label follows every spoken message.
